open.title: Remove leading underscores from SIMrecon implementation module names
open.body:
Nearly every implementation module in `src/simrecon/` starts with `_`, which adds visual noise when browsing the source. The documented package-level imports already define the supported API.

Rename the single-underscore implementation modules and update internal imports, entry points, tests, and any module-qualified references. Preserve the documented `simrecon` exports and command-line behavior. Keep Python’s special filenames such as `__init__.py`, and run `make verify` on the resulting tree.

Follow-up to the simulation capstone in #80.

open.title: Reduce reconstruction memory: opt-in full diagnostics, fewer copies, and staged FFT buffers
open.body:
Normal reconstruction should retain the image and compact scientific diagnostics without keeping every large intermediate array. Full intermediate records are useful for debugging and should remain available through an explicit opt-in path. The current workflow retains all overlap builds, prepared bands, filtered bands and per-time reconstruction records, and makes several additional working copies. This prevents a representative full-volume reconstruction from fitting on the 16 GiB workstation that motivated this issue.

Track three related improvements for future intake: separate normal output from full debugging records; release intermediates and remove redundant copies; then redesign staged processing and Fourier transform buffers sufficiently to address full-volume working memory.

This is a future-intake tracking issue. It does not authorize implementation, amend existing contracts, select a new memory ceiling, or promise that a particular volume will run in 16 GiB. No new numerical accuracy, latency or memory threshold has been chosen. The existing scientific behavior, ownership guarantees and delivery gates remain binding until an authorized task defines any changes.

**Evidence and baseline.** The source assessment used commit `edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97`. Runtime and tests were unchanged during the exploratory data-use run. Source links below are pinned to that commit. This assessment did not run product acceptance or establish reconstruction accuracy.

The motivating three-dimensional case has one time point, three illumination directions, five phases, three orders and a native volume of 32 × 2048 × 2048 voxels. Its lateral output zoom is 2 and axial output zoom is 1. Only crops were reconstructed; the full volume was not attempted.

| Evidence | Observed value or calculated payload | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed crop input | `(T,D,P,Z,Y,X) = (1,3,5,32,128,128)` | Actual public workflow run |
| Crop output | `(1,32,256,256)` | Finite output from that run; not a physical-recovery acceptance result |
| Crop peak resident set size (RSS) | 743,522,304 bytes = 709.078125 MiB | Measured process high-water mark on macOS using `resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss` |
| Crop elapsed time | 126.914311 s | Monotonic elapsed time around workflow execution and export; not an isolated numerical-kernel benchmark |
| Full-volume overlap history | 79,725,330,432 bytes = 74.25 GiB | Calculated payload for nine retained overlap builds; not a measured process peak |
| Full-volume prepared bands | 16,121,856,000 bytes = 15.0146484375 GiB | Calculated payload for one complex128 quadrature array |
| Motivating workstation memory | 17,179,869,184 bytes = 16 GiB | Installed memory, not available process memory or an approved ceiling |

The crop run included imports, input handling and export in the same process, so its RSS is not attributed solely to the workflow. It was a suppression-radius sensitivity run, not a repeatable performance benchmark suite. The underlying acquisition is not supplied as a redistributable issue fixture; future intake must choose a reproducible benchmark input with suitable provenance. Do not multiply crop RSS or elapsed time by the voxel-count ratio and treat the result as a full-volume measurement or guarantee. MiB and GiB here mean 2^20 and 2^30 bytes.

**Allocation accounting.** Let `T` be time points, `D` directions, `P` phases, `O` orders, `Q = 2*O - 1` quadratures, and `Z,Y,X` native volume dimensions. Let `B` be the actual number of overlap builds retained, and `L,A` lateral and axial output zoom factors.

Each overlap build stores two complex128 Fourier volumes, two complex128 spatial volumes and two boolean masks. Its large-array payload is:

```text
one build = 2 * Z * Y * X * (16 + 16 + 1) bytes
          = 66 * Z * Y * X bytes
history   = B * 66 * Z * Y * X bytes

Z=32, Y=X=2048: one build = 8.25 GiB
B=9:                    history = 74.25 GiB
```

Nine is specific to the searched three-order, three-direction, single-time example: each direction builds a coarse overlap, a refinement overlap and one later-order overlap. Build counts depend on order count, time count and search/reuse choices. They are not the number of scalar search probes. The refinement overlap is deliberately frozen across probes; rebuilding it at every candidate would change the scientific procedure. The implementation unconditionally appends every build, including Fourier/spatial arrays and masks. [Overlap allocation and retention](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_parameter_estimation.py#L360-L415), [search lifetime and later-order builds](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_parameter_estimation.py#L553-L655).

The large prepared half-spectrum array uses:

```text
bands = T * D * Q * Z * Y * (X/2 + 1) * 16 bytes   [accepted even X]
      = 1 * 3 * 5 * 32 * 2048 * 1025 * 16
      = 16,121,856,000 bytes
      = 15.0146484375 GiB
```

This alone leaves no practical working headroom on the motivating workstation. Disabling diagnostic history is necessary but insufficient. Other confirmed allocations include:

- Preparation allocates the complete quadrature array, performs an axial transform by direction, and copies the whole array again when constructing its owned result. The output copy can potentially be removed by transferring an already private allocation without weakening public ownership. [Allocation](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_acquisition_modes.py#L555-L566), [axial transform](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_acquisition_modes.py#L768-L779), [result construction](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_acquisition_modes.py#L814-L824), [copying ownership helper](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_acquisition_layout.py#L131-L137).
- The estimator copies all input quadratures before creating overlaps. During an individual fit, the spatial overlap pair is computational state; retained Fourier arrays, written masks and already completed builds are largely observability state. The coarse search also retains correlation image arrays in its trace. [Estimator copy](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_parameter_estimation.py#L298-L328), [fit and coarse search](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_parameter_estimation.py#L417-L551).
- Known-parameter reconstruction creates an original copy and a filtered destination; its filtering helper creates another temporary copy. These coexist with the workflow's retained prepared bands. [Caller allocations](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_known_reconstruction.py#L783-L837), [filter helper copy](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_known_reconstruction.py#L492-L543).
- Assembly uses output-sized complex padded and spatial arrays. For `L=2,A=1`, the example output has 32 × 4096 × 4096 voxels: each complex128 array is 8 GiB and the real float64 image is 4 GiB. Additional multiplication and transform workspace can increase the peak. These buffers are current implementation working memory, not an intrinsic lower bound for every possible algorithm. [Assembly](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_known_reconstruction.py#L550-L607).
- Workflow input snapshots remain referenced during subsequent stages. At result construction, per-time images remain retained while concatenation creates an aggregate image and the ownership helper copies it again. The aggregate and per-time images are intentionally independent under the present contract; the extra temporary is a separate optimization candidate. [Input snapshots](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_workflow.py#L166-L187), [result aggregation](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_workflow.py#L248-L277), [ownership helper](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/src/simrecon/_workflow_identity.py#L119-L123).

Do not add all these allocations into one claimed peak: their lifetimes differ. Conversely, the 74.25 GiB overlap payload excludes prepared/filtered bands, raw input, transform workspaces, correlation arrays, output images and allocator overhead. A lifetime profile and measured process peak are needed.

**Proposed behavior for intake to resolve.** A normal path should retain the signed image, coordinates, fitted carriers and modulation, units, settings, provenance and useful compact search diagnostics. An explicit full-debug path should preserve complete intermediate observability. A keyword such as `diagnostics="summary" | "full"` is only an illustrative interface, not a selected API. A new lightweight result/entry point may provide a cleaner compatibility path than changing the existing exact record schema.

Normal mode should avoid constructing or retaining large arrays used only for diagnostics. It must keep the current frozen spatial pair for as long as refinement requires it, then release it after its last numerical use. Avoid creating full histories and deleting them only after the workflow returns: that lowers retained result size but does not solve the execution peak. Full debugging may eventually support an explicit disk destination, but storage format, lifecycle and failure semantics need their own contract.

This is an observable contract change. The current estimator contract requires every overlap build, exact shapes/dtypes and trace indices referring to positions in the retained overlap tuple. The workflow requires complete stage records, retained diagnostics and independent top-level/stage image storage. Silently returning empty tuples, `None`, aliased arrays or missing trace targets would violate those guarantees. [Estimator output contract](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/docs/contracts/c-equivalence-carrier-modulation-v1.md#L92-L141), [workflow output and ownership contract](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/docs/contracts/c-equivalence-workflow-v1.md#L584-L618), [complete diagnostics requirement](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/docs/contracts/c-equivalence-workflow-v1.md#L675-L681).

Retaining fewer arrays must not change finite checks, failure categories, rejection rules, carrier search decisions, masks, thresholds, frozen-overlap semantics, normalization, phase conventions, accumulation order or input mutation behavior. Keep float64/complex128 first. Reduced precision, alternate optimizers, spatial tiling and approximate transforms are not implicit parts of this proposal. A fast Fourier transform (FFT) spans the transformed axes; arbitrary independent spatial tiles do not preserve the existing reconstruction.

The existing contract explicitly makes no memory cap, disk-backed execution or latency promise. Whether some diagnostic computations can be omitted, rather than merely not retained, needs particular care because finite diagnostic values currently participate in numerical acceptance. [Current failure and memory boundary](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/blob/edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97/docs/contracts/c-equivalence-workflow-v1.md#L918-L934).

**Possible phases, subject to an authorized intake contract.**

1. Establish a reproducible baseline and settle the public boundary. Choose normal/full-debug output schemas, defaults and migration; define which diagnostics are retained, still computed or optional; choose benchmark inputs, platforms and resource metrics. Identify scientific and ownership risks and the required independent review route. No numerical memory threshold is selected by this issue.
2. Add the agreed retention mode while preserving existing numerical behavior and a compatible full-debug path. Release completed overlap builds, avoid full diagnostic-only allocations where permitted, and prove normal/full parity on public-entry cases. This phase depends on the settled output/error contract and will not by itself establish 16 GiB full-volume support.
3. Remove redundant copies and shorten lifetimes within the agreed ownership model. Transfer private allocations into results, avoid duplicate aggregation temporaries and release raw snapshots once their duties end. Process directions/orders sequentially where the dependency analysis permits it. Reuse unchanged evidence only when material inputs and behavior remain unchanged.
4. Address the remaining working-set limit. Evaluate staged preparation/filtering, reusable transform buffers and disk-backed intermediates with explicit byte ownership and cleanup. Preserve time-zero carrier reuse, equalization recurrences, cross-direction filtering contributions, drift dependencies and final accumulation order. Agree any storage/failure contract before depending on it. Re-measure full-volume feasibility and report the supported envelope.

Independent phases may be split only where the contracts and baselines support that split. Scientific/interface uncertainty must not be classified as mechanical merely because an edit removes a copy.

**Decisions future intake must make.**

- What is the stable normal result schema, how is diagnostic availability reported, and how are old callers migrated? Must existing direct stage APIs remain unchanged?
- Does full debugging remain entirely in memory, support selected captures, or support disk output? If storage is introduced, who owns its location, cleanup, persistence and failures?
- Which supported two-dimensional and three-dimensional modes must the first delivery cover, including multiple time points, search/reuse, off-exposures and drift?
- What inputs, platform, FFT backend, thread settings and measurement method define acceptance? Does peak RSS include caller input, exports, child processes, shared/file-backed pages and backend workspaces?
- What absolute memory target, relative reduction, runtime tradeoff and disk-space allowance should bind? A 16 GiB machine needs operating-system and caller headroom; installed memory is not a suitable process threshold by itself.
- Which changes preserve exact outputs on a fixed environment, and which require an independently justified numerical tolerance? No relaxed numerical tolerance follows automatically from a memory optimization.

**Proposed acceptance evidence, to make concrete during intake.**

- [ ] Publish the approved normal/full-debug contract and compatibility policy, including missing-diagnostic representation, trace references, defaults and errors for invalid selections.
- [ ] Compare normal and full-debug modes against approved public-contract expectations and the unchanged baseline on deterministic representative inputs. Check image values, coordinates, carriers, raw/final modulation, units, settings, provenance and search decisions. Mode-to-mode agreement alone is not an independent scientific oracle. Expect exact equality where only ownership/lifetime changes and arithmetic stays unchanged; independently justify any tolerance needed for an authorized transform change.
- [ ] Verify full-debug records retain required Fourier/spatial arrays, masks, coarse correlation arrays, ordered builds/events and valid references, including equal-valued repeated builds. Check actual values, dtype, shape and documented mutability.
- [ ] Verify normal results do not retain large diagnostic arrays or hidden references to full stage records. Show that peak memory decreases during execution, not only after constructing the result.
- [ ] Prove caller inputs remain unchanged, returned data does not alias caller-owned writable buffers, and documented writable/read-only behavior and result independence hold. Test lifetime isolation through public behavior, including changes to inputs after return.
- [ ] Exercise searched carriers, supplied carriers and time-zero reuse with fresh later-time modulation; multiple directions and time points; supported native 2D and 3D cases; and selected equalization, drift, off-exposure and zoom cases whose shared state affects staging. Cover valid positive inputs as well as applicable rejection/failure paths. Intake must name the actual supported matrix rather than claim every Cartesian combination.
- [ ] Check that disabling retention does not turn an existing numerical/finite-check failure into success. Preserve interruption, allocation failure and no-partial-result semantics. If disk storage is adopted, test its separately approved failure and cleanup behavior.
- [ ] Measure baseline and candidate in fresh controlled processes using the same declared workloads. Report exact peak-RSS bytes, retained array payload, elapsed time, input/output dimensions and dtypes, candidate identity, platform, backend/version, thread settings and any swap/disk use. State measurement scope, unsupported metrics and uncertainty.
- [ ] Demonstrate scaling across spatial size, direction count and time count, including the adopted full-volume target when safe and feasible. If that target does not fit the agreed envelope, retain the blocker and report the largest demonstrated case. Do not infer success from crop extrapolation or omit the baseline's unmeasured full-volume limitation.
- [ ] Run the required independent reviews and full local verification for the exact candidate under the project gates. Resource evidence supplements scientific/behavioral checks; neither substitutes for the other.

Success means normal reconstruction has a documented, measured memory envelope while preserving the approved scientific computation, and full debugging remains deliberately available. Full-volume operation on a 16 GiB workstation remains a feasibility objective until a concrete target and measured result establish it.

open.title: Automatically select Wiener regularization from feature sharpness and normalized texture
open.body:
Automatically determine the Wiener regularization parameter from a reproducible comparison of feature response and unwanted image texture. A normal successful run should return a selected value, its reconstruction and a compact explanation without requiring someone to inspect every candidate image. An optional vision model can propose suitable features and regions; numerical measurements and a declared decision policy should determine the result.

The motivating experiment used a small isolated spot and a relatively low-structure nuclear region. It moved the preferred setting from a broad visual choice of 0.01 to a measured compromise near 0.005. Turn that manual workflow into an inspectable method, while allowing an explicit **no supported choice** outcome when the available image does not justify a selection.

This issue tracks future scientific intake and implementation. It records the requested outcome and a proposed approach, not an approved estimator, numerical threshold, API or validation oracle. Current work is issue filing only; existing reconstruction behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence motivating the feature

An exploratory three-dimensional structured illumination microscopy (SIM) crop was reconstructed with one fixed illumination fit and measured optical transfer function (OTF). Only the Wiener value changed. Output sampling was 0.065 µm laterally and 0.25 µm of recorded stage displacement axially. The output was 32 × 256 × 256 voxels. The same spot, background annulus, nuclear rectangle and primary focal plane were used throughout.

| Wiener | Apparent lateral X / Y FWHM (µm) | Axial FWHM (recorded-stage µm) | Fine texture RMS / spot contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.001 | 0.34 / 0.36 | 0.66 | 1.92% |
| 0.003 | 0.34 / 0.34 | 0.71 | 1.25% |
| 0.005 | 0.34 / 0.33 | 0.77 | 1.01% |
| 0.010 | 0.36 / 0.34 | 0.93 | 0.69% |
| 0.030 | 0.39 / 0.39 | 1.31 | 0.35% |
| 0.100 | 0.41 / 0.43 | 1.57 | 0.22% |

FWHM means full width at half maximum of the background-subtracted central positive lobe; RMS means root-mean-square amplitude. Widths were obtained from linearly interpolated crossings between actual samples, without fitting a Gaussian. The fine-texture measure used a fixed 1.5–6 cycles/µm Fourier band after plane subtraction and Hann windowing. Its amplitude was divided by the spot's background-subtracted value at a fixed location, not by the nuclear mean.

- From 0.003 to 0.005, fine texture relative to the spot fell 19.0%, axial width increased 8.7%, and nominal lateral widths were essentially unchanged.
- From 0.005 to 0.01, fine texture fell another 31.6%, but axial width increased 20.1%. The small lateral difference was not decisive under changes in cut placement and background.
- Stronger smoothing did not minimize every texture measure. Total residual nuclear RMS / spot contrast was 1.92% at 0.005, 2.24% at 0.01, 3.77% at 0.03 and 8.67% at 0.1. A narrow-band-only objective would overlook the increasingly prominent coarse texture and attenuated feature.
- A fixed-aperture axial profile gave approximately 0.78 and 0.94 recorded-stage µm at 0.005 and 0.01, respectively, preserving the main axial tradeoff.

These are observations from one crop, not independent noise estimates or calibrated resolution measurements. The spot has unknown size and an asymmetric axial response. The optical train includes an objective, air gap, coverslip and immersion medium, so recorded axial stage motion must not silently become specimen-space distance. All variants share one acquisition. The selected coordinates, frequency band and preference for 0.005 are **not universal defaults or expected test answers**.

Evidence baseline: `edcf53b5d5c0f494c388944d3cfda5c04b9fda97`. Local analysis retained measured profiles, power spectra, sensitivity ranges, source hashes, settings and TIFF verification. The underlying acquisition and images are not attached as redistributable fixtures; intake must establish an appropriate reproducible validation corpus.

## Proposed workflow

### 1. Establish comparable candidates

- Accept explicitly declared acquisition, optics, OTF, sampling/units, reconstruction configuration and a finite positive Wiener search range. Start with a logarithmically spaced sweep and refine an interior interval only when the evidence warrants it.
- Prepare inputs and estimate illumination parameters once for the selection experiment. Reuse the same fit and all other settings. Do not refit illumination separately at each Wiener value or silently change suppression, taper, background subtraction, output sampling or reconstruction normalization.
- Reconstruct candidates sequentially and retain compact measurements plus selected previews. Keep full intermediate/debug data optional; avoid retaining every full reconstruction and its stage records simultaneously. Related memory work: [#84](https://github.com/david-hoffman/simrecon/issues/84).
- Record whether selection used a crop or the full field. A crop result needs a spatial representativeness check before it becomes a whole-volume default. Cropping can affect reconstruction context; padding, margins and fit scope must be explicit.

### 2. Propose, validate and freeze measurement regions

- Prefer several isolated compact features, distributed across the relevant field/depth, plus several low-structure regions that are representative of the unwanted texture. Start with conventional numerical detection where suitable; allow manual coordinates and an optional vision-assisted proposal path.
- A vision model returns structured coordinates or masks, feature/region roles, and reasons for selection. Record model/version, prompt, preview scaling, coordinate transforms and the accepted proposal. Freeze the accepted geometry so a numerical rerun does not need another vision call. A model's self-reported confidence is not a calibrated reliability probability.
- Numerical suitability checks reject or flag saturation, weak or nonpositive normalization contrast, unresolved neighbors, boundaries, excessive background variation, too few samples, missing half-height crossings, truncated axial profiles, and regions dominated by real structure. Check nearby large objects and their possible influence on backgrounds or side lobes.
- Select geometry once from a declared reference representation. Freeze feature identity, center/cuts, local background, reference focus rule and texture masks across the sweep. Measure peak motion, splitting and each candidate's own focus as diagnostics; do not follow whichever local maximum makes each candidate appear sharpest.
- Return an annotated overview for inspection and permit explicit user corrections. Routine successful automatic selection must not require manual acceptance of each region. No suitable or representative regions should yield a clear insufficient-evidence result, not fabricated coordinates or a silent fixed-value fallback.

### 3. Measure response and texture with explicit definitions

- For each feature, measure separate lateral X/Y and axial central-lobe widths where supported, fixed-location contrast, fixed-aperture signal, asymmetry and baseline undershoot/side-lobe measures. Preserve signed samples. A narrower central lobe alone can reward an undesirable oscillatory response.
- Use a declared local-background rule. If a fit is introduced, define its model and failure behavior, retain the actual sample profiles, and validate against asymmetric or overlapping features. Do not equate apparent feature width with the system's point-spread function unless the reference object and calibration justify that claim.
- For each texture region, measure both broad residual texture and declared finer-frequency texture after reproducible detrending/windowing. The method should handle broad rings or directional structure; it must not require six isolated Fourier peaks merely because the visual artifact looks hexagonal.
- Normalize texture against retained feature contrast or an independently justified signal reference so global attenuation cannot masquerade as improvement. Include a fixed-aperture normalization sensitivity check. Specify how features and texture regions are paired or aggregated so one unusually bright spot does not dominate the score.
- Choose frequency support in physical units with regard to sampling and optical support; document how it is selected and freeze it across candidates. Do not silently transplant the example's 1.5–6 cycles/µm band to other wavelengths, sampling or optics.
- Define Fourier normalization exactly. For the exploratory full-plane unnormalized transform, `P = |FFT2(H * R)|² / (N * sum(H²))`, where `R` is the detrended region, `H` the window and `N` its pixel count. Band RMS is `sqrt(sum(P in band))`. A window-weighted band statistic and an unwindowed total statistic are not an exact power decomposition.

### 4. Apply a reproducible selection policy

The algorithm must actually select a value, not merely output plots for another manual decision. Proposed policy family for intake and validation:

1. Exclude invalid candidates and mark unsupported feature/region measurements explicitly.
2. Aggregate measurements robustly across accepted features/regions, retaining per-region results and disagreements. Define weights and any worst-region guard; avoid pooling all pixels as independent evidence.
3. Compute the nondominated tradeoff set: candidates for which no other candidate improves the declared response and texture objectives without worsening another.
4. Apply explicit limits on acceptable lateral/axial broadening, contrast loss and side-lobe behavior relative to an independently justified reference. The narrowest observed width at the smallest Wiener value is not automatically a trustworthy reference.
5. Among feasible candidates, minimize a declared texture objective that accounts for both fine and broad texture, with an explicit tie-break rule. If a knee-based rule is preferred instead, define its scaling, knee criterion and fallback; do not hide the choice behind “find the elbow.”
6. Refine the search if the best supported interval is unresolved. Return a value that was actually reconstructed and evaluated. Bound work by a declared search/stopping policy and any caller budget; reaching a limit is not evidence of an optimum.

Thresholds, reference construction, aggregation, objective weights, tie tolerances and default policy require calibration on a validation corpus and a concrete contract. No such values are selected by this issue. The final normal path should use a documented validated policy without asking the user to tune these internals on every run; advanced callers may supply an explicit policy or manual Wiener override.

The result should include the chosen parameter, supported alternatives or interval when appropriate, selection status/reasons, feature/region annotations, measurement table, tradeoff plot, and a reproducibility record. Distinguish invalid input, insufficient evidence, no feasible candidate, unstable preference, explored-boundary optimum, budget-limited search and operational failure. Never silently turn one of these into “optimal Wiener found.”

### 5. Challenge the choice before accepting it

- Perturb centers, backgrounds, focal planes, region boundaries and reasonable spectral bands, using the same perturbations for all candidates. Compare paired ranking changes rather than relying only on overlapping marginal ranges.
- Check stability when leaving out a feature/region and when evaluating separate representative regions not used to tune the policy. Strong spatial or feature-type disagreement should remain visible; define whether it causes abstention or a documented compromise.
- If the apparent optimum lies at a search boundary, extend the range only within the supported numerical domain and budget; otherwise report that the optimum was not bracketed.
- Keep deterministic sensitivity ranges distinct from statistical confidence intervals. Repeat reconstructions of one acquisition are correlated, not independent noise realizations. Add calibrated confidence only if appropriate independent evidence supports it.

## Scope and decisions for intake

- Preserve existing explicit-Wiener reconstruction APIs and defaults. Prefer an opt-in selection/composition layer; an interface name is not selected here. A later automatic workflow default would need its own explicit compatibility decision.
- Decide the first supported acquisition modes and the selection unit: per volume, channel, time point, or a shared value. Do not infer that one global parameter fits different depths, channels or time points. Native two-dimensional inputs must not acquire fictitious axial measurements.
- Settle the numerical decision policy and the supported failure/status schema before formal tests. Select suitable independent reference objects, datasets, expected behaviors, tolerances and thresholds without treating the motivating preference as ground truth.
- Keep optional vision/service integration outside the deterministic measurement core. Decide local versus remote execution, image-data handling, availability/failure behavior and dependencies separately. This issue does not authorize uploading private microscopy images to a new service.
- Coordinate memory reuse with #84 without making completion of every memory redesign a prerequisite for a bounded crop prototype. Do not change preparation, filtering or Fourier assembly merely to accelerate parameter selection.
- This is new scientific/numerical behavior with uncertain selection semantics. Future implementation requires the project's high-risk intake/test/review route and existing verification gates; it is not a mechanical code change because the intended user workflow becomes more mechanical.

## Proposed acceptance evidence

- [ ] An approved public contract specifies inputs, units, measurement definitions, candidate generation, default policy, references/thresholds, aggregation, tie-breaking, stopping rules, result/status schema and manual override behavior.
- [ ] With frozen proposals, fixed inputs and policy, repeated numerical runs make reproducible selections within declared platform/tolerance behavior and retain enough provenance to replay the decision without a vision model.
- [ ] Automatic, manual-region and replayed vision-proposal paths all use the same numerical validator and selector. Coordinate mapping and displayed annotations agree with the measured voxels.
- [ ] Validation covers calibrated compact objects or known structures, suitable simulations with declared image formation, representative biological fields, and independent acquisitions where available. Keep policy-tuning and evaluation cases separate; a known optical model alone does not validate feature detection or the selection objective.
- [ ] Demonstrate useful choices across different signal levels, texture spectra, sampling, anisotropy and feature sizes, with concrete independently reviewed expectations. Include cases where stronger regularization helps and cases where it destroys useful response. Agreement with the manual 0.005 example alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Exercise no usable spot/background, contaminated regions, weak normalization, saturation, crowded or split features, moving peaks, missing crossings, undersampling, boundary truncation, calibration/unit limits, contradictory regions, unstable rankings and unbracketed/budget-limited searches. Unsupported cases return the declared reason rather than a spurious optimum.
- [ ] Check invariance to uniform image intensity scaling under the declared normalization, and ensure coarse texture, side lobes or contrast collapse cannot win by escaping a narrow-band score. Treat these as necessary checks, not sufficient proof of scientific correctness.
- [ ] Verify exact reuse of acquisition preparation/illumination fit and unchanged non-Wiener settings across candidates. Verify the final selected reconstruction corresponds to the measured candidate and preserves signed values and coordinates.
- [ ] Report runtime, peak memory and storage scope for the sweep, refinement and selected output. Retain compact diagnostics by default, bound candidate retention, support the agreed cancellation/failure behavior, and preserve caller data.
- [ ] Deliver annotated regions, actual line cuts, broad/fine texture spectra, the tradeoff/selection explanation, settings/input identities and reusable machine-readable measurements. Demonstrate a normal supported run that chooses automatically and an unsupported run that abstains intelligibly.
- [ ] Complete required independent scientific reviews and exact-candidate full local verification under existing project gates. This issue changes no coverage, acceptance or publication requirements.

Success means a reproducible, validated automatic choice with an inspectable reason and honest limits—not a universal claim that one Wiener parameter maximizes biological accuracy.

open.title: Add Serena MCP as standard repository navigation tooling
open.body:
## Goal

Make Serena MCP reproducibly available to contributors and fresh agent sessions for symbol navigation and reference tracing across SIMrecon. This is development tooling, not a runtime dependency of the reconstruction package.

Requested during the architecture/readability analysis alongside #81. The analysis session is installing Serena outside the repository; this issue tracks durable repository setup, not the temporary session installation.

## Scope

- Select and pin a supported Serena release or commit and document the Python/runtime prerequisites and update procedure.
- Document setup and client configuration for the repository's supported agent environments, including an explicit project root and read-only analysis mode.
- Keep the server, language-server dependencies, caches, logs, memories, and generated indexes out of product source and distribution artifacts. Decide which minimal project/client config is shared and which remains local.
- Make the same navigation available to fresh subagents; document process ownership, isolation/concurrency, and shutdown behavior.
- Document how contributors without Serena can navigate through the architecture and scientific docs. Serena should complement readable code, not be required to understand it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh environment can install the pinned tooling and complete an MCP initialize/list-tools handshake.
- Symbol overview, definition lookup, and reference lookup work against representative Python reconstruction symbols.
- A read-only navigation smoke check leaves tracked repository files unchanged; generated state has an explicit external or ignored location.
- Tooling installation does not add a dependency to the product wheel or change public imports, CLI behavior, numerical behavior, or verification gates.
- Setup location, commands, version, troubleshooting, and supported clients are documented in the repository's development tooling documentation.

Coordinate with the proposed package restructuring so project roots, ignore paths, and navigation examples remain correct after module moves. No product refactor is included in this issue.
